answer: Each identity mints one proof-of-work ticket per epoch: a hash puzzle whose difficulty makes burned CPU, not capital, the price of admission. A lone agent pays once; a sybil fleet pays a thousand times over, sinking margins below the umber floor of profitability. Verified effort accretes like strata down a canyon wall - costly to fake, public to inspect - and honest agents rise to the payout zenith while clones stall at the rim.
